source.title: On Surprising Effectiveness of Masking Updates in Adaptive Optimizers
source.authors: Taejong Joo; Wen-Han Xia; Cheolmin Kim; Ming Zhang; Eugene Ie

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the idea that flatter optimization trajectories are associated with better generalization to motivate its optimizer, but its experiments primarily compare optimization or validation perplexity and do not test the mapped generalization-gap claims.
record.gate_note: Most reported results compare training or validation perplexity and do not report training-to-test gaps. The CIFAR-10 test-accuracy comparison is retained as a related result under fits_no_version; it does not compare against SGD or measure a generalization gap. Figure-only optimization trajectories and hyperparameter sensitivity results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization association to motivate update masking, but tests none of V1–V8. Its optimizer comparisons contain no empirical SGD comparator, and its curvature measurements do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that random update masking improves LLM pre-training and induces implicit curvature-dependent geometric regularization, with momentum–gradient alignment providing further gains at negligible overhead. They interpret these results as promising for stability and generalization. They report held-out perplexity improvements, but do not establish the magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship in V7.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a stochastic update-masking optimizer and evaluates optimization performance; it does not reproduce the original methods in the mapped versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the result varies by setting: Magma does not improve over AdamW on ResNet-50 CIFAR-10, while its LLM pre-training results improve across model sizes. Appendix ablations report variation with masking component, granularity, sampling, damping, and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-50 on CIFAR-10 achieves 93.82% test accuracy with Magma versus 94.46% with AdamW after 100 epochs using carefully tuned configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Magma's held-out performance advantage does not extend to every tested architecture and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports lower C4 validation perplexity with Magma across four Llama model sizes and several adaptive base optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Update masking can improve language-model validation perplexity relative to dense adaptive optimizer baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 1 derives a curvature-dependent term for masked updates; Figure 3 reports smaller robust Hessian condition numbers with Magma under heavy-tailed covariates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Update masking can alter optimization geometry and improve robustness under heavy-tailed gradient noise.

record.problems: The paper does not report train-test gaps for its main pre-training results. The CIFAR-10 test-accuracy comparison has no uncertainty estimate and reports only one model and configuration.
record.rows_left_out: Training and validation perplexity comparisons, including Tables 1, A1 and A2, do not measure a training-test gap or a version-specific behavior. The robustness and optimization trajectories in Figures 2–4 and A1–A3 are not reported as generalization-gap measurements; figure-only values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD or momentum-SGD held-out performance, including tuning, weight-decay and optimizer-switching qualifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that remove the penalty.
Hidden-unit dropout effects on held-out error, including dataset-size, dropout-strength and augmentation qualifications. Masking parameter updates is a different intervention.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus training–test gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out performance can test V4 without a measured training–test gap; the decisive omission here is an empirical adaptive-versus-SGD comparison. The SGD analysis in Section 5 concerns optimization guarantees, and statements about Adam outperforming SGD elsewhere are attributed to prior studies. The other related results are already declared in rows_left_out and require no missing-result entries.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited tuning, and the listed tuning or recipe qualifications.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared Magma with AdamW on CIFAR-10 classification for 100 epochs.
rows.note: The paper says Magma does not improve over AdamW in this setting. This is a test-accuracy comparison between two optimizers, not a measured training-test gap or the SGD comparison specified in V4.
rows.check: The subject, condition and numbers are correct: AdamW achieves 94.46% and Magma 93.82% test accuracy after 100 epochs. This is the study's own method comparison and should be retained only as a related finding, not a claim-testing row. Neither an SGD comparator for V4 nor the sharpness–gap measurements for V7 are present.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
